title: Barry Switzer's Back-to-Back National Titles: Oklahoma 1974 and 1975
question: Did Oklahoma win back-to-back national championships under Barry Switzer?
answer: Yes. Switzer's 1974 Sooners went 11-0 and won the AP national title despite a bowl ban, and the 1975 team repeated at 11-1 after beating Michigan 14-6 in the Orange Bowl.
summary: Barry Switzer's Sooners won national titles in 1974 and 1975, one under a bowl ban and one capped by a 14-6 Orange Bowl win over Michigan. Here's the story.
body: Barry Switzer was only in his second season as Oklahoma's head coach in 1974, and his team was under NCAA probation for recruiting violations. The penalties kept the Sooners out of bowl games and off network television, and they were ineligible for the coaches poll. None of it slowed them down. Oklahoma went 11-0, led the nation in scoring at 43 points per game and finished No. 1 in the AP poll.

That roster was loaded. Running back Joe Washington, brothers Lee Roy and Dewey Selmon on the defensive front, and All-American linebacker Rod Shoate helped the team produce eight All-Americans, the most in any OU season up to that point.

The 1975 season brought one painful afternoon. Unranked Kansas won 23-3 in Norman on Nov. 8, snapping a 28-game Oklahoma winning streak. The Sooners regrouped, and on Jan. 1, 1976, they beat Michigan 14-6 in the Orange Bowl in Miami, with quarterback Steve Davis running for one of the touchdowns. This time Oklahoma finished No. 1 in both the AP and coaches polls.

Lee Roy Selmon won the Outland Trophy and the Lombardi Award that year and went first overall in the 1976 NFL draft to Tampa Bay. Switzer added a third national title in 1985 and finished his 16 seasons at OU with a 157-29-4 record and 12 Big Eight championships. He later coached the Dallas Cowboys to a Super Bowl title, and he was inducted into the College Football Hall of Fame in 2001.
